 J Ud Gme N T

Yeshwanthpur Police has filed charge-sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 304B r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec. 4 of D.P.Act.
 2.
The facts are as under:
The accused No.1 is the mother-in-law of the deceased.
The marriage of the deceased with son of accused No.1 was solemnized on 30.05.2013.
Thereafter, the deceased was residing with her husband in House No.969/3, Diwakarapalya, Gokula Extension, Yeshwanthpur.
The accused No.1 along with accused No.2, started to harass the deceased and demanded Rs.10 Lakh as dowry.
Without bearing the cruelty, dowry harassment and torture, on 13.06.2016 at about 6.15a.m, in the above stated house, the deceased poured kerosene, set fire and succumbed to burn injuries.
The accused No.1 is responsible for her death.
Hence this charge sheet.
3. The accused No.1 is on bail.
4. The charge has been framed against the accused No.1.
The accused No.1 has denied the charge and claims to be tried.
5. The prosecution has examined its witnesses as P.W.1 to P.W.6.
The documents are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
C.W.17 & C.W.26 are reported as dead.
State Of Karnataka vs Akashavani on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147006191/
The learned prosecutor has requested to summon C.W.2 to C.W.12, C.W.15, C.W.18 to C.W.24.
The material witnesses are turned hostile.
Hence the prayer made by the prosecution is rejected.
Evidence is taken as closed.
6. The statement of the accused No.1 U/s.313 of Cr.P.C. is recorded.
The accused No.1 has denied incriminating evidence and not chosen to lead defence evidence.
7. Heard arguments.

8. The points that arise for my consideration are:
 1.
Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage of son of accused No.1 with the deceased, the accused No.1 & 2, demanded dowry of Rs.10 Lakh and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 4 of D.P.Act?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage of son of accused No.1 with the deceased, the accused No.1 & 2 with common intention, demanded dowry of Rs.10 Lakh, treated the deceased with physical and mental cruelty and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 498A r/w 34 of IPC?
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that unable to bear dowry harassment, cruelty and torture by the accused persons, on 13.06.2016 about 6.15a.m, in House No.969/3, Diwakarpalya, Gokula Extension, Yeshwanthpur, the daughter-in-law of accused No.1 had poured kerosene, set fire on herself, committed suicide and accused No.1 is responsible for her death and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 304B r/w 34 of IPC?
4. What order?

9. My answer to the above points are as hereunder:
Points No.1 to 3 : In the Negative Point No.4 : As per final order for the following:
:R E A S O N S:

3 10.
Points No.1 to 4:
All the points involve common discussion.
C.W.1 is a complainant and mother of the deceased.
She deposed as P.W.1.
She has denied the alleged dowry demand.

According to her,
the deceased was in good terms with her husband and the accused persons.
She has stated that, her daughter had accidentally contacted with fire while heating milk and died due to burn injuries.
She is not aware of contents of the complaint.
It is marked as Ex.P.1.
The learned prosecutor has treated the complainant as hostile and cross-examined.

The witness has denied the contents of Ex.P.1.
11.

C.W.13 & 14 are the younger sisters of the deceased and they have been examined as P.W.2 &
P.W.3.
Their evidence is similar to that of their mother.
They have failed to support the prosecution.

At the time of cross-examination by the prosecutor, both have denied the contents of the statement marked as per Ex.P.2 & Ex.P.3.
12.
C.W.16 is a relative of the deceased and he deposed as P.W.4.
According to him, the deceased was leading happy marital life in her husband's house.
He has denied the alleged dowry harassment.
Since he has turned hostile, the prosecutor has cross- examined.

He has denied the contents of the statement marked as per Ex.P.4.
13.
C.W.25 has deposed as P.W.5.

He had received the complaint, registered the case, reported FIR as per Ex.P.5 and transferred the investigation papers to C.W.26.
14.
C.W.27 has been examined as P.W.6.
He had collected the accidental register extract from Victoria Hospital as per Ex.P.6.
Postmortem report is marked as Ex.P.7.
He had conducted mahazar as per Ex.P.6 and prepared rough sketch as per Ex.P.13.

He had recorded the statement of C.W.8 &
9 and requested Thasildar to conduct inquest.
The requisition is marked as Ex.P.14.

He had arrested the accused No.1 and recorded the voluntary statement as per Ex.P.15.
15.
I.O has deposed that, based on Ex.P.15, he had conducted seizure mahazar as per Ex.P.7 and seized the jewels.
According to him, he handed over the said articles to the elder brother of the deceased, recorded the statement of C.W.10 to C.W.12 and further statement of C.W.1.
He had collected the receipts showing the purchase of jewels.
They are marked as Ex.P.16.
He had recorded the statement of C.W.3 to C.W.7.

He had received postmortem report as per Ex.P.17.
16.
I.O. has stated that, C.W.26 is no more and he can identify the signature.
Ex.P.8 is spot mahazar.
Rough Sketch is marked as Ex.P.9.
The marriage Invitation card and marriage photos are marked as per Ex.P.11 and P.12.
Seizure panchanama is marked as Ex.P.10.

Inquest mahazar is marked as Ex.P.13.
17.
The learned prosecutor has requested to summon the remaining witnesses.
The material witnesses are failed to support the prosecution.
No purpose will serve, if the remaining witnesses are examined.
Hence, the request of the prosecution is rejected.
18. It is pertinent to note that, the family members and the relatives of the deceased have turned hostile.
There are no materials to connect the incident with accused No.1.
The prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused No.1.

Hence, without any option, I answered all the points in the State Of Karnataka vs Akashavani on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147006191/
4 Negative.
19.
Point No.5:
From the discussion made herein above, I proceed to pass the following:
ORD ER

Acting under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Section 498A, 304B r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.4 of D.P.Act The bail bond executed by the accused No.1 and the surety bond shall stand cancelled.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on the computer, corrected by me and then pronounced in open Court on this the 16th day of February, 2023)
(K.S.Jyothishree)
